오빠.m: older brother (of a female); older male friend (of a female)
오빠.x: My older brother is three years older than me.
오빠.e: In K-dramas also for male idols.
오빠.t: Only females say 오빠. It's also used for an older boyfriend or a close older male friend.

부엌.x: My mother is cooking in the kitchen.
부엌.t: Pronounced [부억] alone, but 부엌에 → [부어케]: the ㅋ links to the next vowel.

나무.ex: 우리 집 앞에 큰 나무가 있어요.
나무.x: There's a big tree in front of our house.
나무.e: Means tree and wood. 소나무 = pine tree; 나뭇잎 = leaf.

슬퍼하다.m: to be sad, to grieve, to mourn
슬퍼하다.x: The child was very sad when the puppy died.

지루하다.x: That class was so long that it was boring.
지루하다.t: 지루하다 means something is tedious; 심심하다 means you're bored with nothing to do.

옷장.x: I put my winter clothes away in the closet.
옷장.e: Native 옷 (clothes) + 장 (cabinet). -장 = cabinet: 책장, 신발장.
옷장.t: Pronounced [옫짱] — the ㅈ becomes tense after the final consonant.

전부.m: all, everything, the whole; (as adverb) all
전부.x: I finished all the homework I got today.

도움.x: With my friend's help, I finished moving quickly.
도움.e: Noun made from 돕다 (to help): 도우- + -ㅁ.

한번.forms: 한번 -아/어 보세요 = Give it a try
한번.ex: 제가 만든 김치찌개를 한번 드셔 보세요.
한번.x: Try the kimchi stew I made.
한번.e: 한 'one' + 번 'time' — but often just softens a suggestion.
한번.t: Write 한번 for 'try, sometime' but 한 번, with a space, for literally 'one time'.

이런.x: In weather like this, I want to stay home.
이런.e: Short for 이러한, from 이렇다 'to be like this'.
이런.t: Said alone, 이런! is a mild 'Oh no!' or 'Darn!'

진지.e: Native Korean honorific word for 'meal', with no hanja.
진지.t: The plain word is 밥; use 진지 for grandparents and other elders, with 드시다 or 잡수시다 instead of 먹다.

그러게요.m: I know, right?; exactly; I wonder (agreeing)
그러게요.x: I know, right? It's really hot today.
그러게요.e: From 그러다 'to be so' + the ending -게, roughly 'that's just it'.
그러게요.t: Used to agree with what someone just said. It can also mean 'I wonder': 그러게요, 왜 안 올까요? 'I wonder why they're not coming.'

발급받다.m: to get (a document or card) issued, to receive
발급받다.x: I got a new card issued at the bank.
발급받다.t: The office 발급하다 (issues it); you 발급받다 (receive it).

예매.ex: 인기 있는 공연은 예매가 빨리 끝나요.
예매.x: Tickets for popular shows sell out quickly.
예매.t: 예매 is buying tickets ahead; 예약 is reserving a table, room or appointment.

효도.m: filial piety, being a good son or daughter
효도.ex: 부모님께 효도하고 싶어서 여행을 보내 드렸어요.
효도.x: I wanted to do something for my parents, so I sent them on a trip.
효도.e: Literally 'the way of filial piety' — a core Confucian value in Korea.
효도.t: 효도하다 is used for any act of caring for parents, like a gift or a call.

화해하다.x: Today I made up with the friend I fought with yesterday.
화해하다.t: Not related to 화 (anger); use N와/과 화해하다 for 'make up with N'.

발견하다.x: Scientists discovered a new star in space.
발견하다.t: 발견하다 is finding what already exists; 발명하다 is inventing something new.

사용법.x: Please tell me how to use this machine.
사용법.e: -법 = way or method of doing it: 사용법, 요리법, 공부법.
사용법.t: Pronounced [사용뻡] — the ㅂ of 법 is tensed here.

소개되다.m: to be introduced, to be featured
소개되다.ex: 이 식당은 텔레비전에 여러 번 소개되었어요.
소개되다.x: This restaurant has been featured on TV several times.

의존.ex: 스마트폰에 대한 의존이 점점 심해지고 있어요.
의존.x: Dependence on smartphones is getting more and more serious.

시절.ex: 대학 시절에 친구들과 여행을 많이 했어요.
시절.x: In my college days, I traveled a lot with friends.
시절.t: It usually refers to a past period, often with nostalgia: 그 시절 (those days).

불합격.m: failure (of an exam or selection), rejection
불합격.ex: 시험에 불합격해서 내년에 다시 볼 거예요.
불합격.x: I failed the exam, so I'll take it again next year.
불합격.t: In everyday speech people usually say 시험에 떨어졌어요 instead of 불합격했어요.

와플.x: I ordered an ice cream waffle at the café.
와플.t: Street-stall 와플 in Korea is often folded around whipped cream and jam.

간부.x: The company's senior staff gathered for a meeting.
간부.e: Literally 'trunk part' — the core people holding up an organization.

체결.m: signing, conclusion (of a contract or treaty)
체결.x: The two companies signed the contract today.
체결.t: Common collocation: 계약을 체결하다 (to sign a contract).

게시하다.m: to post, to put up (a notice)
게시하다.x: We posted the exam schedule on the school website.
게시하다.t: 게시하다 is formal; for your own social media posts, people usually say 올리다.

재수.m: studying a year to retake the college entrance exam
재수.ex: 원하는 대학에 떨어져서 재수를 하기로 했어요.
재수.x: I didn't get into the college I wanted, so I decided to retake the exam next year.
재수.t: Don't confuse it with 재수 'luck': 재수 없다 means 'unlucky' or, rudely, 'obnoxious'.

임대.x: The first floor of this building is leased out as shops.
임대.e: Literally 'lend for rent'. The owner does 임대; the tenant does 임차.
임대.t: A sign saying '임대' on an empty shop means 'for rent'.

활달하다.ex: 우리 딸은 성격이 활달해서 친구가 많아요.
활달하다.x: My daughter has a lively personality, so she has lots of friends.
활달하다.e: Literally 'lively and getting through' — energetic and free-spirited.

웬만하면.m: if possible, if it's not too much trouble, unless there's a good reason
웬만하면.x: If possible, please send it by tomorrow.

참조하다.ex: 더 자세한 내용은 저희 홈페이지를 참조하세요.
참조하다.x: For more details, please refer to our website.
참조하다.t: 참조 also means 'cc' in emails; 참고하다 is the more common everyday word.

갈다.forms: 갈아요 · 갈았어요 · 갈 거예요 · 가세요 (ㄹ drops)
갈다.m: to replace, to change; to grind, to sharpen
갈다.x: The fluorescent light burned out, so I replaced it with a new one.
갈다.e: Homonyms: 갈다 means 'replace', 'grind', and also 'plow' — context tells them apart.
갈다.t: 갈 거예요 and 가세요 look like forms of 가다 'to go', so rely on context.

우수하다.ex: 그 학생은 성적이 우수해서 장학금을 받았어요.
우수하다.x: That student got a scholarship for excellent grades.

이상형.ex: 제 이상형은 잘 웃고 친절한 사람이에요.
이상형.x: My ideal type is someone who smiles a lot and is kind.
이상형.e: 이상 'ideal' + 형 'type': the kind of person you'd love to date.
이상형.t: A classic question on dates and TV shows: 이상형이 어떻게 되세요? 'What's your ideal type?'

파문.x: The minister's remarks caused a huge stir.
파문.e: Literally 'ripple pattern' on water — an image for spreading consequences.

반어.m: irony (verbal), saying the opposite of what you mean
반어.x: The phrase "Well done" is used ironically here.

배치되다.m: to run counter to, to contradict
배치되다.x: That policy runs counter to the spirit of the constitution.
배치되다.e: Literally 'gallop with backs turned' — heading in opposite directions.
배치되다.t: A homonym 배치 (different hanja) means 'placement, deployment': 군대가 배치되다.

가다듬다.m: to compose (oneself), to collect; to tidy up, to refine
가다듬다.ex: 발표 전에 숨을 고르고 마음을 가다듬었어요.
가다듬다.x: Before the presentation, I caught my breath and composed myself.
가다듬다.e: Related to 다듬다 'to trim, polish' — putting yourself back in order.

매진하다.m: to devote oneself to, to push forward with, to strive toward
매진하다.x: After graduation, I plan to devote myself entirely to research.
매진하다.e: Literally 'stride forward' — pressing on toward a goal.
매진하다.t: Homonym alert: a different 매진 means 'sold out', as in 표가 매진되다 'tickets are sold out'.

취임.ex: 새 시장은 취임 후 첫 회의를 열었습니다.
취임.x: The new mayor held the first meeting after taking office.

원한.ex: 그는 오래된 원한 때문에 복수를 결심했어요.
원한.x: Because of an old grudge, he resolved to take revenge.
원한.t: Common pattern: 원한을 품다 (to harbor a grudge) and 원한을 사다 (to earn someone's grudge).

전란.ex: 많은 문화재가 전란 중에 불에 타 버렸습니다.
전란.x: Many cultural treasures were burned during the war.
전란.t: Pronounced [절란] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ (liquidization).

저항력.x: Getting enough sleep strengthens your body's resistance to disease.
저항력.e: Literally 'power to resist and oppose'. -력 = power or ability: 능력, 기억력.
저항력.t: Pronounced [저항녁] — nasalization of ㄹ after ㅇ.

매도하다.m: to denounce, to condemn, to vilify
매도하다.x: Some media outlets denounced him as a traitor.
매도하다.t: A homonym 매도하다 means 'to sell' in finance (주식을 매도하다); context decides.

되새기다.m: to reflect on, to go over again in one's mind; to chew the cud
되새기다.ex: 선생님의 조언을 마음속으로 여러 번 되새겼어요.
되새기다.x: I went over my teacher's advice in my mind many times.
되새기다.e: 되- 'again' + 새기다 'to chew the cud'; 되새김질 is what cows do.

원로.m: elder, senior figure, veteran (in a field)
원로.ex: 그 원로 배우는 50년 넘게 연기를 해 왔어요.
원로.x: That veteran actor has been acting for over 50 years.
원로.e: Literally 'first and old' — the most senior elders.
원로.t: Pronounced [월로] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

험담.m: badmouthing, slander, speaking ill of someone
험담.ex: 다른 사람의 험담을 하는 건 좋지 않아요.
험담.x: It's not good to badmouth other people.
험담.t: 험담하다 is the verb; casual younger speakers often say 뒷담화하다 or 뒷담 까다 instead.

빌미.m: pretext, cause, opening (for something bad to happen)
빌미.ex: 작은 실수가 상대 팀에게 공격의 빌미를 주었어요.
빌미.x: A small mistake gave the other team an opening to attack.
빌미.t: Typical patterns: 빌미를 주다 (give someone an opening) and 빌미로 삼다 (use as a pretext).

공공재.ex: 도로와 국방은 누구나 이용하는 대표적인 공공재입니다.
공공재.x: Roads and national defense are classic public goods that everyone uses.

싱숭생숭하다.m: to feel restless, fidgety, unable to settle (often from spring or excitement)
싱숭생숭하다.x: Now that spring's here, I feel restless for no reason.
싱숭생숭하다.e: Playful rhyming mimetic word; the bouncing sounds mirror a fluttering, unsettled heart.
싱숭생숭하다.t: Lighter than 뒤숭숭하다: often a pleasant, distracted restlessness, especially in spring.

표준편차.ex: 표준편차가 작으면 데이터가 평균 근처에 모여 있어요.
표준편차.x: If the standard deviation is small, the data is clustered near the mean.

침전.ex: 두 용액을 섞자 바닥에 하얀 침전이 생겼어요.
침전.x: When the two solutions were mixed, a white precipitate formed at the bottom.
침전.t: Weather 'precipitation' is 강수, not 침전; 침전 is only for settling particles.

작가정신.ex: 이 작품에서는 타협하지 않는 작가정신이 느껴집니다.
작가정신.x: You can feel an uncompromising artistic integrity in this work.
작가정신.e: Literally 'writer spirit' — commitment to one's art over money or fame.
작가정신.t: Pronounced [작까정신]; 작가 always has a tense ㄲ sound.

비녀.ex: 할머니는 머리를 쪽 찌고 비녀를 꽂으셨어요.
비녀.x: Grandma put her hair up in a bun and slid in a hairpin.
비녀.e: A married woman's hairpin, worn through the chignon (쪽머리); jade and silver were prized.
비녀.t: The verb is 꽂다 (stick in): 비녀를 꽂다.

서명운동.ex: 주민들이 공원을 지키기 위해 서명운동을 벌였어요.
서명운동.x: Residents launched a petition drive to save the park.
서명운동.t: Collocation: 서명운동을 벌이다 'to launch a petition drive'.
